info.title: AWS CodePipeline

requests.description: Returns information about a specified job and whether that job has been received by the job worker. Used for custom actions only.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.AcknowledgeJob
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Confirms a job worker has received the specified job. Used for partner actions only.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.AcknowledgeThirdPartyJob

requests.description: Creates a new custom action that can be used in all pipelines associated with the AWS account. Only used for custom actions.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.CreateCustomActionType
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description:
Creates a pipeline.

In the pipeline structure, you must include either artifactStore or artifactStores in your pipeline, but you cannot use both. If you create a cross-region action in your pipeline, you must use artifactStores.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.CreatePipeline
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description:
Marks a custom action as deleted. PollForJobs for the custom action fails after the action is marked for deletion. Used for custom actions only.

To re-create a custom action after it has been deleted you must use a string in the version field that has never been used before. This string can be an incremented version number, for example. To restore a deleted custom action, use a JSON file that is identical to the deleted action, including the original string in the version field.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.DeleteCustomActionType
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Deletes the specified pipeline.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.DeletePipeline
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Deletes a previously created webhook by name. Deleting the webhook stops AWS CodePipeline from starting a pipeline every time an external event occurs. The API returns successfully when trying to delete a webhook that is already deleted. If a deleted webhook is re-created by calling PutWebhook with the same name, it will have a different URL.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.DeleteWebhook
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Removes the connection between the webhook that was created by CodePipeline and the external tool with events to be detected. Currently supported only for webhooks that target an action type of GitHub.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.DeregisterWebhookWithThirdParty
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description:
Returns information about a job. Used for custom actions only.

When this API is called, AWS CodePipeline returns temporary credentials for the S3 bucket used to store artifacts for the pipeline, if the action requires access to that S3 bucket for input or output artifacts. This API also returns any secret values defined for the action.

requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description:
Returns information about the state of a pipeline, including the stages and actions.

Values returned in the revisionId and revisionUrl fields indicate the source revision information, such as the commit ID, for the current state.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.GetPipelineState
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description:
Returns information about any jobs for AWS CodePipeline to act on. PollForJobs is valid only for action types with "Custom" in the owner field. If the action type contains "AWS" or "ThirdParty" in the owner field, the PollForJobs action returns an error.

When this API is called, AWS CodePipeline returns temporary credentials for the S3 bucket used to store artifacts for the pipeline, if the action requires access to that S3 bucket for input or output artifacts. This API also returns any secret values defined for the action.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.PollForJobs
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.PollForThirdPartyJobs
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Defines a webhook and returns a unique webhook URL generated by CodePipeline. This URL can be supplied to third party source hosting providers to call every time there's a code change. When CodePipeline receives a POST request on this URL, the pipeline defined in the webhook is started as long as the POST request satisfied the authentication and filtering requirements supplied when defining the webhook. RegisterWebhookWithThirdParty and DeregisterWebhookWithThirdParty APIs can be used to automatically configure supported third parties to call the generated webhook URL.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.PutWebhook
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Resumes the pipeline execution by retrying the last failed actions in a stage. You can retry a stage immediately if any of the actions in the stage fail. When you retry, all actions that are still in progress continue working, and failed actions are triggered again.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.RetryStageExecution
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Starts the specified pipeline. Specifically, it begins processing the latest commit to the source location specified as part of the pipeline.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.StartPipelineExecution
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values

requests.description: Stops the specified pipeline execution. You choose to either stop the pipeline execution by completing in-progress actions without starting subsequent actions, or by abandoning in-progress actions. While completing or abandoning in-progress actions, the pipeline execution is in a Stopping state. After all in-progress actions are completed or abandoned, the pipeline execution is in a Stopped state.
requests.name: POST /#X-Amz-Target=CodePipeline_20150709.StopPipelineExecution
requests.note: Replace {{AWS_CODEPIPELINE_API_KEY}} with your API key | Replace path parameters (e.g. {{VOICE_ID}}) with actual values
